title: Evolution Strategies at the Hyperscale
claim: Structured low-rank perturbations are cheap to form and feed into the model function, in place of full-rank random noise.
layout: Thin horizontal strip, left-to-right, outer-product equation feeding a function f(·)
description: The crop is a thin horizontal strip cut from the middle of a larger schematic, so most of the figure is missing. Its centre shows a column vector and a row vector, drawn as small heatmap grids in purple-to-orange. An equals sign leads to a full square heatmap in the same colours, which is their outer product (a low-rank matrix). A long black arrow then points to f( green grid + σ · purple-orange grid ), meaning a weight matrix plus a scaled low-rank perturbation passed through a function. At the top edge there are partial arrows and coloured blocks. A dashed vertical line and the start of a curved line on the right suggest further panels, perhaps a plot. The eye goes first to the colourful matrices.
caption: Schematic visualisation of EGGROLL using N workers.
abstract: Evolution Strategies (ES) is a class of powerful black-box optimisation methods that are highly parallelisable and can handle non-differentiable and noisy objectives. However, naÃ¯ve ES becomes prohibitively expensive at scale on GPUs due to the low arithmetic intensity of batched matrix multiplications with unstructured random perturbations. We introduce Evolution Guided GeneRal Optimisation via Low-rank Learning (EGGROLL), which improves arithmetic intensity by structuring individual perturbations as rank-$r$ matrices, resulting in a hundredfold increase in training speed for billion-parameter models at large population sizes, achieving up to 91% of the throughput of pure batch inference. We provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of Gaussian ES for high-dimensional parameter objectives, investigating conditions needed for ES updates to converge in high dimensions. Our results reveal a linearising effect, and proving consistency between EGGROLL and ES as parameter dimension increases. Our experiments show that EGGROLL: (1) enables the stable pretraining of nonlinear recurrent language models that operate purely in integer datatypes, (2) is competitive with GRPO for post-training LLMs on reasoning tasks, and (3) does not compromise performance compared to ES in tabula rasa RL settings, despite being faster.
